title: Rock reaches the bottom as rock
question: Does what lands on the pond floor read as broken rock now rather than as a dune of grit? Both clips are the same drop, at true speed.
context_md:
*"Chunks of rock hit the water and then start disintegrating into grit instead of tumbling down as rock chunks."*

That is fixed. The same 600-cell slab, same drop:

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| what is left of the slab | **nothing** --  |  |
| still stone when it stops | 0 of 600 | **422 of 600** |
| times the same rock was broken | 4.2 | **1.5** |

**What was doing it.** A piece lifted out of the grid left the space it was standing in marked *empty*, so water poured into its own footprint. It then found water in front of it with nowhere to put it -- only 2,834 of 10,849 attempts to shove water aside succeeded -- gave up after three frames, was written back into the world, was judged unsupported, and was broken up again. Over and over, all the way down.

A body moving one cell **vacates exactly as many cells as it enters**, so the water in front can be handed the space behind by arithmetic instead of by searching for a gap. There is no failure left in that path, so nothing stalls, so nothing gets re-broken.

**Three things it cost on the way, and none of them showed up in a test.** It ate 920 cells of water before I filtered one set; it left permanent wedge-shaped air pockets standing inside the pond, which the water ledger was perfectly happy about because nothing had been *lost* -- only the picture showed it; and holding the footprint from the moment a piece breaks off made a scene with **no water in it at all** five and a half times slower per frame, because more rock survives intact and the load model's cost grows faster than the piece does. So a piece only takes its footprint when there is liquid within forty-eight rows below it, and every dry scene is byte-identical.

**What I have not fixed:** the last of it still shatters -- you will see a puff of grit in the water on the way down, and the mound at the bottom has gravel between the blocks. Say if that is still too much.

items.label: before
items.caption: Every one of the 600 cells ends as powder. The floor is a smooth dune.

items.label: now
items.caption: 422 of 600 still stone. The floor is jagged.
